evidence_articles.title: Names of people belonging to Matua, minority communities deleted from post-SIR voter rolls: Mamata - The Hindu
evidence_articles.rephrased: **Mamata Banerjee**, West Bengal Chief Minister, accused the **Union government** of targeting specific communities by deleting names from voter rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) proce
evidence_articles.content: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Tuesday (April 7, 2026) alleged that names of people belonging to the Matua and minority communities were deleted from the post-SIR voter rolls in the State. Addressing a rally at Chakdaha in Nadia district, Ms. Banerjee said that the TMC will stand by those whose names were excluded from the voter rolls, following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. Assembly elections April 7, 2026 LIVE: Campaigning ends in Kerala, Assam, Puducherry today According to the latest data by the Election Commission of India (ECI), nearly 91 lakh voters have been deleted from the electoral rolls in West Bengal after the SIR process. The poll panel is yet to announce the finally altered voter base for the state after the roll revision process. As per official data released on February 28, 63.66 lakh names, around 8.3% of the electorate, were deleted since the SIR process began in November last year, reducing the voter base from about 7.66 crore to just over 7.04 crore. Accusing the Centre of discrimination, Ms. Banerjee alleged that names were being removed from voter rolls by targeting specific communities. “Why this discrimination? You are excluding Matuas, Rajbanshis and minorities. Do you think that people do not understand this?” the CM said. She also claimed that in districts with significant minority population such as Murshidabad, Malda and North Dinajpur, names were “picked and removed like lice” from the electoral rolls. Ms. Banerjee asserted that following her intervention in the Supreme Court, around 32 lakh names out of nearly 60 lakh cases under ‘adjudication’ had been restored. “Those whose names are still missing should apply before the tribunal. The TMC will stand by you and provide legal support,” she said. Questioning the Centre’s stand on infiltration, Ms. Banerjee said the Union government has the responsibility of protecting the country’s borders, but it was blaming the West Bengal government for infiltration. Describing the upcoming Assembly polls as a battle to protect people’s identity and democratic rights, the TMC supremo urged voters to respond through the ballot. “This election is a fight to save your democracy, language and respect so that no one can ever call you a foreigner,” Ms. Banerjee said. At another poll rally in Bongaon, the CM asserted that the Trinamool Congress will win more seats than before, and form government for the fourth consecutive term. “The TMC will ultimately win and get more seats than before,” she said. The party had won 215 seats in the 2021 elections for the 294-member West Bengal assembly. “This election is to avenge the deletion of names from the voter list,” Ms. Banerjee said. The TMC chief claimed that names of 300 members of Missionaries of Charity, which was formed by Mother Teresa, have been deleted in the electoral rolls revision exercise, and also those of monks of the Ramakrishna Mission and Bharat Sevasram Sangha. Ms. Banerjee also said that several names have been excluded from the rolls in Murshidabad, Uttar Dinajpur, Malda, South 24 Parganas and Nadia districts, while reiterating that in Bhabanipur constituency, where she is contesting for re-election, 40,000 names have been struck off. “We will have to see how many names have been restored in the supplementary list... I will not allow detention camps to be set up (in Bengal). Constitutional rights must be given, and I will continue to fight for restoration of these,” she said. In a bid to woo the Matua community, who have a strong presence in several assembly constituencies in North 24 Parganas and Nadia district, Ms. Banerjee said that her government has initiated a lot of development works in those areas. The CM also accused the BJP of trying to divide Matua community votes. Attacking Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Ms. Banerjee claimed that he had lunch with leaders of Gulf countries and hugged them, with religion not becoming a barrier. “When you go to Gulf countries, you hug the Muslim rulers,” she said. Ms. Banerjee also claimed that cattle are exported from the country, but it does not become an issue as to whether that is right or wrong. “Their (BJP) religion is to divide votes, that is not Hinduism,” the TMC chief added. Published - April 07, 2026 02:08 pm IST

recent_articles.title: K.T. Jaleel, wife join CPI(M), calls it ‘stand against communal forces’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **K.T. Jaleel**, former Kerala Minister, and his wife Fathimakutty have joined the **CPI(M)** after losing his Assembly seat in recent elections.  Jaleel cited West Bengal's decline as a warning against weakening the Left front and attributed the rise of the Trinamool Congress to the Communist party's decline. He emphasized that he chose to join the **CPI(M)** as an act of resistance against forces spreading communal hatred within communities, claiming it is part of a global effort to weaken communist parties.  Jaleel believes individuals can be both believers and communists and cited countries like Iran, China, Russia, and North Korea as examples.

recent_articles.title: Kerala to Bengal, Why India’s Left Is Facing an Existential Crisis
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Communist Party of India (Marxist)**, once a dominant force in Indian politics, has lost significant power across several states.  This decline is attributed to the party's failure to adapt to the digital age and its inability to effectively engage with voters on social media platforms like WhatsApp. The BJP, meanwhile, has successfully leveraged these platforms for communication and mobilization, capturing public attention through nationalist narratives and coordinated online campaigns. This shift in political dynamics underscores a broader trend of the Left failing to address contemporary issues such as inequality and precarity, leaving it vulnerable to criticism and losing its ability to connect with ordinary citizens.

recent_articles.title: Mango The Sweet Diplomat, From Mughals To Modern India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Americans** are embracing **Kesar mangoes**, a popular Indian fruit, after a long-standing ban was lifted in 2006. This trend began with then President George Bush's appreciation for the fruit during a visit to India and has continued through subsequent years of diplomatic exchanges between the two countries.  The tradition of gifting mangoes dates back centuries, from Mughal emperors who used them as diplomatic tools to modern-day leaders like **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** who have received gifts of mangoes from other nations. The practice continues today with **President Pranab Mukherjee**, **Sheikh Hasina**, and others using mangoes as a symbol of goodwill between their countries.

The protest included the raising of "Jai Bangla" slogans outside the local TMC candidate's residence and election office.

recent_articles.title: M.P. Assembly passes resolution to implement women’s reservation after delimitation amid uproar by Opposition - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Madhya Pradesh** Assembly passed a resolution to implement women's reservation following the delimitation exercise, despite opposition from the Congress.  **Chief Minister Mohan Yadav** proposed the resolution, urging immediate implementation after the completion of the delimitation process. The resolution was met with resistance from the Opposition, who argued that the government's actions contradicted its words and called for an immediate enforcement of the Women's Reservation Act.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal election 2026: Mood of Bengal suggests BJP victory in polls, will return during oath-taking ceremony: PM Modi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** addressed a rally in Barrackpore, West Bengal on the final day of campaigning for the Assembly elections. He expressed confidence that the **BJP** would form the next government and asserted his intention to return for the oath-taking ceremony after May 4th.  **Modi** accused the ruling **TMC** of presiding over “syndicate raj”, political violence, and economic decline, while promising employment opportunities for youth and a focus on restoring West Bengal's prosperity. recent_articles.title: NCSC seeks report on Mamata Banerjee's alleged 'derogatory' remark against SC community - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC)** has taken suo motu cognisance of a video clip allegedly showing West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee using derogatory language against the SC community during an election rally. The NCSC has directed the Chief Secretary and Director General of Police to submit a detailed report within three days, warning that they may issue summons if no response is received. **NCSC Chairman Kishor Makwana** condemned the alleged remarks as "unfortunate" and stated that such incidents are punishable under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The BJP has also criticized Ms. Banerjee's comments, accusing her of being anti-Dalit and anti-SC.

recent_articles.title: TMC lodges complaint against BJP candidate over alleged misuse of national flag - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **TMC** filed a complaint against **BJP** candidate Papia Adhikari for allegedly using the national flag during her campaign in Tollygunge.  The complaint, filed by **Kohinoor Mazumdar**, TMC spokesperson and vice-president of the West Bengal Trinamool Chhatra Parishad, alleges that Ms. Adhikari used a dupatta bearing the Indian tricolour while campaigning and wiped her face with it. The police are examining the complaint.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool running a reign of terror in West Bengal, says Rahul Gandhi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, senior Congress leader, accused the **Trinamool Congress (TMC)** of running a reign of terror in West Bengal ahead of the state assembly election.  He condemned the murder of **Debdeep Chatterjee**, a Congress worker, allegedly by TMC-affiliated goons and called for immediate action against those responsible. The Congress has demanded justice and security for the victim's family while maintaining its commitment to non-violence.

recent_articles.title: BJP attacking Bengali culture, pride: Kejriwal; Modi won’t have his way in Bengal: Tejashwi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Arvind Kejriwal**, former Delhi Chief Minister and convener of the **Aam Aadmi Party**, joined the Trinamool Congress campaign in West Bengal on Sunday, addressing three rallies in Kolkata and Howrah.  His visit coincides with the final days of campaigning for the second phase of the Assembly elections, scheduled to conclude Monday evening. The AAP recently experienced a setback as seven of its MPs switched to the **Bharatiya Janata Party**.

recent_articles.title: As campaign reaches a crescendo, Modi reaches out to Matuas, Mamata camps at Bhabanipur - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** campaigned in West Bengal, emphasizing the BJP's commitment to citizenship for the Matua community of Hindu refugees from Bangladesh. **Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee** held a roadshow in her Bhabanipur constituency, criticizing voter deletions and the Election Commission-appointed administration. She warned that those involved in such actions would face consequences.

recent_articles.title: Two women’s quest for justice for their daughters fuels Bengal poll fight - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Two mothers from West Bengal, **Ratna Debnath** and **Sabina Yasmin**, are contesting the Assembly elections to seek justice for their daughters' deaths. **Debnath**, whose daughter was murdered in a hospital attack, is campaigning on behalf of the **BJP**.  **Yasmin**, whose daughter died in a bomb attack during victory celebrations, is running as a candidate for the **Left Front**. Both mothers blame the ruling **Trinamool Congress** and Chief Minister **Mamata Banerjee** for their daughters' deaths. Their campaigns highlight concerns about political violence and accountability within the state.

recent_articles.title: Nrusimha Sagar reservoir non-operational due to pending compensation to displaced families: BJP - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Gudur Narayana Reddy**, a senior leader of the **BJP**, has called for immediate payment of pending compensation, relief, and rehabilitation (R&R) benefits to families displaced by the Nrusimha Sagar Reservoir. The reservoir, completed in 2023 under the Kaleshwaram project, remains unused despite its capacity to store around 11.39 TMC due to unresolved compensation issues.

recent_articles.title: BJP committed to women's security, Trinamool ‘stands with goons who torture women’: PM Modi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** accused the **Trinamool Congress** of sheltering criminals who harm women, citing the BJP's support for Rekha Patra and the mother of an RG Kar victim as proof of its commitment to women's safety.  He also announced that all refugees fleeing religious persecution in neighboring countries would be granted citizenship through the Citizenship Amendment Act procedures.

recent_articles.title: ECI suspends police officials in Bengal; Trinamool alleges strongroom breach - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** has suspended five police officials in West Bengal's Diamond Harbour and deployed 11 new observers following allegations of a strongroom breach during the first phase of the Assembly election. The commission also ordered disciplinary proceedings against the officers for their alleged misconduct and failure to maintain neutrality.

recent_articles.title: Jadavpur University got global acclaim despite fiscal crunch: Teachers’ body on PM’s critical remark - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** criticized **Jadavpur University** in West Bengal, calling it a symbol of anarchy under the TMC's rule.  However, the **Jadavpur University Teachers' Association (JUTA)** refuted these claims, stating that the university has been recognized globally as a center of excellence despite financial constraints and played a significant role in social justice. JUTA also accused the government of neglecting the university's funding needs and undermining public institutions while supporting private ones.

recent_articles.title: Assembly Elections 2026 LIVE: No repoll ordered in Tamil Nadu, West Bengal says ECI officials - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India (ECI)** has concluded that no repoll is necessary in any of the polling stations for the West Bengal and Tamil Nadu assembly elections held on April 23, 2026.  **The ECI** suspended five officers in **West Bengal** for alleged misconduct during the election process. **Abhishek Banerjee**, national general secretary of the Trinamool Congress (TMC), believes the party is leading in the first phase of voting and predicts a "century" of victories.

recent_articles.title: Record turnout in West Bengal poll fuels rival claims, data tempers conclusions - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The first phase of the West Bengal Assembly Elections on April 23, 2026, saw a record-breaking voter turnout of 92.88%, exceeding previous highs in 2011 and 2006.  **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Home Minister Amit Shah**, and **West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee** all claimed victory for their respective parties. Retired bureaucrat and former Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal Jawhar Sircar expressed uncertainty about the impact of the high turnout, attributing it to both voter anger over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process and a potential shift in voting patterns among migrant workers. The second phase of the elections is scheduled for April 29th.

recent_articles.title: BJP staring at electoral losses in West Bengal, Tamil Naidu, Kerala: Farooq Abdullah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Dr. Farooq Abdullah**, president of the **National Conference**, predicted electoral victories for the Congress party in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, while also stating that the BJP would likely experience losses in West Bengal and Tamil Nadu during the 2024 elections.  He attributed this to the people's rejection of divisive politics.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal election: Modi promises fresh probe into R.G. Kar case after election; Mamata says BJP will get ‘zero’ in many districts - The Hindu

He also highlighted the BJP's commitment to ensuring prosperity for women in West Bengal.  **Union Home Minister Amit Shah** predicted a strong BJP victory, citing anti-incumbency and atrocities on women as key factors.  **Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee**, contesting from Bhabanipur, countered these claims, asserting that the BJP would receive "golla (zero)" in several districts.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal election 2026: Record turnout of over 92% in first phase amidst isolated incidents of violence - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **West Bengal** registered a record voter turnout of 92.03% in the first phase of Assembly elections on April 23, 2026.  The high turnout was attributed to the election being seen as a fight for voting rights and the potential implementation of the National Register of Citizens (NRC). **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** congratulated voters and praised the Election Commission of India (ECI) for ensuring a peaceful election. Despite the record turnout, isolated incidents of violence were reported across different districts, including clashes between supporters of political parties and attacks on BJP candidates.  The second phase of polling will be held on April 29th.

recent_articles.title: SC asks if ED is arguing 'failure of constitutional machinery' in WB by claiming rule of law breach - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** paused the **ED's** rejoinder in a case involving alleged rule-breaking by West Bengal officials during an ongoing raid on the I-PAC premises.  Justice N.V. Anjaria questioned the ED's assertion of "breakdown of constitutional machinery" in relation to the controversy, prompting concern from the court.

recent_articles.title: Congress files complaint against polling violations in Bharatpur constituency - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** party agents in Bharatpur Assembly Constituency filed a complaint with the **West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer**, alleging forceful removal by **Trinamool Congress** workers from multiple booths during the ongoing first phase of polling.
